name: Tank Yard v2.1.5
body:
# Tank Yard v2.1.5

Tougher bosses, smoother bosses online, tank settings for the central server's owner, and a Bastion that acts only on proof. Everything in [v2.1.4](https://github.com/RobertFlexx/tankyard/blob/v2.1.5/docs/releases/v2.1.4.md) is included.

## Bosses

- **Trapper** no longer waits in a corner to be worn down. It has 55% more health, moves faster, fights from closer in and throws a tight, fast pair of traps. When it is cornered, it slides out along the walls toward open ground.
- Right after laying its mine pockets, Trapper sends out a spiral: pairs of traps from opposite sides, each pair turned further round and thrown further out. There are eight pairs at first and twelve once it is badly hurt. It holds its other fire until the spiral ends.
- **Guardian, Summoner, Fallen Overlord and Foundry** have more health. Their drones are faster and sturdier, and they head for where you are going rather than where you are. Once hurt, each boss adds a shot to its volleys: Guardian a piercing shard, Summoner twin bullets, Fallen Overlord two seekers and Foundry a heavy shell.
- Online and in parties, bosses no longer stop for a frame each time an update arrives. They move as evenly as they do offline.

<details>
<summary>Sunderworm encounter changes</summary>

Online, the whole body now moves as smoothly as it does offline. When it dies, the body swells and bursts, throwing blood and flesh that stain the floor, and what is left sinks back into the ground. It has a new death sound to match.

</details>

## Central server owner

The verified central owner has a **My tank** tab in the server panel. It changes only their own tank: choose any hull by name or ID, then scale weapon damage from 0.25× to 8× and shot speed from 0.25× to 3×. The settings last for the round and mark the arena as modded. If the owner's verification ends, the server removes their shots and returns their original hull. See [server administration](https://github.com/RobertFlexx/tankyard/blob/v2.1.5/docs/creator-administration.md#the-central-owners-tank).

## Bastion Anticheat

- Bastion now acts only on proof: a request the game's own client never sends, whatever the network does to its packets. Each proof counts once, however many later packets repeat the same bad frame, and three distinct proofs within a minute close the connection. One stray request can't end a session.
- Input frames out of order inside one packet are now a proof.
- Staff requests are checked against game data that a patch can change, so one that fails is refused with a message and never counts as a proof.
- Observe mode records proofs and keeps players connected. When enforcing, each distinct proof gets an audit line before the disconnect.
- Tests replay the game's input stream through loss, duplication, delays of up to three seconds and shuffled delivery, and run a real client over a poor emulated connection across round restarts and a sequence wrap. Neither produces a finding.

See [Bastion Anticheat](https://github.com/RobertFlexx/tankyard/blob/v2.1.5/docs/bastion-anticheat.md).

## Compatibility

Multiplayer still uses **protocol 35**. Tank Yard 2.1.5 and 2.1.0–2.1.4 clients and servers can play together; hosts and players on 2.0 builds still need to update together. The boss changes, Bastion and the **My tank** tab run on the server and arrive when a host updates. Smoother bosses online come with the client. The [hosting guide](https://github.com/RobertFlexx/tankyard/blob/v2.1.5/docs/hosting.md#upgrading-to-215) covers upgrading.

See [bosses](https://github.com/RobertFlexx/tankyard/blob/v2.1.5/docs/bosses-and-learning.md) and [hosting](https://github.com/RobertFlexx/tankyard/blob/v2.1.5/docs/hosting.md).

# Tank Yard v2.1.4

A small visual patch. Everything in [v2.1.3](https://github.com/RobertFlexx/tankyard/blob/v2.1.4/docs/releases/v2.1.3.md) is included.

## Fix

- The Bastion mark in **Credits** now scrolls with its two credit lines. The mark was receiving the menu's scroll offset twice, so it drifted upward faster than the text as the page scrolled. It is now passed in page coordinates like the labels, which apply the offset once when drawing.

## Compatibility

Multiplayer still uses **protocol 35**. Tank Yard 2.1.4, 2.1.3, 2.1.2, 2.1.1 and 2.1.0 clients and servers can play together; hosts and players on 2.0 builds still need to update together.

See [hosting](https://github.com/RobertFlexx/tankyard/blob/v2.1.4/docs/hosting.md), [bosses](https://github.com/RobertFlexx/tankyard/blob/v2.1.4/docs/bosses-and-learning.md) and [modding](https://github.com/RobertFlexx/tankyard/blob/v2.1.4/docs/modding.md).

earlier.name: Tank Yard v2.1.2
earlier.body:
# Tank Yard v2.1.2

Boss fights now finish cleanly, including a killing blow that empties the health bar in one hit. The bar, off-screen pointers and party labels also handle a minimized window and unusually large bosses.

<details>
<summary>Sunderworm encounter changes</summary>

Light rolls across the plates as the body turns. The slits along its flanks breathe, its eyelids close across the eyes, and the mouth opens in overlapping folds around rows of hooked teeth. At the split, both torn ends expose muscle, vessels and bone. A defeated half settles into the floor tail first. Its death sound and effects follow the host’s kill event, so losing sight of a wounded worm cannot trigger a false death.

</details>

## Multiplayer

Once a player has joined, Bastion checks each decoded request against the limits of the negotiated protocol. A control request outside those limits, an input value outside its range, or two copies of the same recent frame that disagree are refused. By default the host discards the message and disconnects that player with a reason; `observe` mode discards and logs it while the player stays connected. Loss, reordering, long gaps and sequence wraparound are ordinary, and the client refuses its own contradictory frames before sending. The action applies only to the connection; players can reconnect.

Hosts can set `bastion_mode = "observe"` to discard invalid requests from joined players and review the findings in the moderation log while those players stay connected. Handshake and malformed-traffic rules are unchanged. See the [host settings](https://github.com/RobertFlexx/tankyard/blob/v2.1.2/docs/bastion-anticheat.md#host-settings).

Multiplayer uses **protocol 35**. Players and hosts on 2.1.x can update independently. The [hosting guide](https://github.com/RobertFlexx/tankyard/blob/v2.1.2/docs/hosting.md#upgrading-to-212) covers upgrades from 2.0.x.

earlier.name: Tank Yard v2.1.0
earlier.body:
# Tank Yard v2.1.0

Harder boss fights, animated health bars, new recorded sound mixes and a rare encounter beneath the arena. Everything in [v2.0.5](https://github.com/RobertFlexx/tankyard/blob/v2.1.0/docs/releases/v2.0.5.md) is included.

**Multiplayer uses protocol 35. Update the host and all players together.** Clients and servers from 2.0 cannot play with 2.1.0. Existing settings, maps, Luau scripts and signed staff packs carry over.

## Boss fights

- Bosses choose between three special attacks according to range, nearby tanks and their target's movement. Each kind has its own priorities, remembers recent attackers and avoids piling onto the same player as every other boss.
- Later phases increase the pressure and shorten openings. Dangerous attacks still have visible warnings, and cover, sharp turns and defensive abilities remain useful.
- Railgunner's cannon and beam require a parry within **75 milliseconds** of pressing the ability while facing the incoming shot, within about **49 degrees**. Its smaller guns keep the normal parry window.
- Rail, plasma, burning shells and steel slugs have distinct clash effects and sounds. The rail clash has a heavier impact.

## Health bars and effects

- Boss health bars blend their colors smoothly, animate incoming damage and leave a glowing white damage trail. A red outline pulses and glows when the boss targets you.
- The headline bar keeps health, phase markers and attack messages visible while the boss moves off screen. Reduced Motion keeps the health information without the decorative flashes and shake.
- Projectile ribbons use finer curves near the camera. Engine exhaust holds its direction through stops and turns.
- Boss arrivals, weapons, parries, rifts and map sound cues use new mixes of recorded metal, stone, steam and creature performances. The recordings are CC0; credits and source details are in the [sound bank reference](https://github.com/RobertFlexx/tankyard/blob/v2.1.0/assets/audio/foley/README.md).

<details>
<summary>Secret encounter: Sunderworm</summary>

Sunderworm is a long, segmented boss with a ground-shaking entrance. Cracks spread before it breaks through the floor, throwing tiles, earth and dust into the air. Its body can be hit only where it is above ground.

- Five phases introduce lunges, bone fans, bile, burrowing, larvae and spine waves. Watch the strike lane and eruption ring before moving in.
- At **16% health**, it tears into a head and tail that fight independently. A surviving half becomes more aggressive. Both must be destroyed.
- Its jaws unfold around hooked teeth, with a contracting throat and saliva strands. Blood streams break into falling droplets, pool on the floor and dry. Torn flesh, debris and blood use the arena's effects and lighting.
- Its health bar shows phase boundaries and warnings before lunges, eruptions and the split. A half's destruction is distinguished from the end of the encounter.
- An eligible natural boss arrival has about a **one-in-two-million** chance of being Sunderworm and needs an arena worth three full-level tanks. The Boss Rush roster rolls a **one-in-24,000** chance when opened. A selected encounter stays in the saved lineup.
- Hosts can explicitly choose `sunderworm` in a Boss Rush lineup or a map Boss trigger. Presentation packs can keep its local roster card available with `"menu": { "bosses": ["sunderworm"] }`.

</details>

## Stability and performance

- Players joining or reconnecting during a worm fight receive its real body positions. Visible segments and collision shapes stay together, and DLSS motion follows each segment's silhouette.
- Bots aim at nearby surfaced body segments and avoid them even when the head is far away.
- A large finishing hit no longer skips the worm's death effects. Exploding rounds cannot trigger their owner's death scene.
- Destroying both halves in the same tick fires encounter-completion logic and the Boss Rush team bonus once. Whole worms reserve room for their tails within the encounter limit.
- Blood, debris and sound queues have fixed limits. Sounds are prepared and cached for playback, and clients receive body positions without the host's full movement history or decision state.

## Updating a server

Install the **2.1.0 server and client together**, along with any separately deployed relay. Protocol 35 is incompatible with protocol 34 from 2.0.0–2.0.5; the connection screen explains which side needs an update.

See [hosting](https://github.com/RobertFlexx/tankyard/blob/v2.1.0/docs/hosting.md), [Pi and Docker upgrades](https://github.com/RobertFlexx/tankyard/blob/v2.1.0/docs/central-pi-upgrade.md), [bosses](https://github.com/RobertFlexx/tankyard/blob/v2.1.0/docs/bosses-and-learning.md) and [modding](https://github.com/RobertFlexx/tankyard/blob/v2.1.0/docs/modding.md).

earlier.name: Tank Yard v2.0.5
earlier.body:
# Tank Yard v2.0.5

A new boss that would prefer you stayed far away, parries that hit back, and a boss bar that finally looks like part of the game.

## Railgunner

- The biggest regular boss, with a lot of health and a heavier cannon than Siege Engine's. It leads moving targets, hunts whoever is furthest away, and is at its worst when you're right under the barrel.
- Its barrel is the warning. A rail shot only strains the latches. When the plasma beam is coming, the armor splits, the coils spread and the muzzle claws unfold, and the whole thing throws open as its aim locks.
- The beam sweeps after its target, then the boss vents with its barrel still open and takes 40% more damage. That's your window.
- It hops backward when crowded and keeps weak flak guns for anyone who gets close.
- It turns up very rarely on its own, and only in arenas with enough experienced players. You can also pick it in a custom Boss Rush, summon it as staff, or practice in **Get under the rail**.

## Parries that hit back

- Parry the beam and it breaks. The stream stops, a bright clash goes off at your tank, and the strike runs back up the line for 10% of the boss's full health.
- Railgunner's cannon goes back as an ion strike (9%), Siege Engine's shell as fire and a blast (7%), and Bastion's slug as a smaller steel-blue hit (4%). Railgunner's lighter echo round is worth half a cannon clash.
- Each clash has its own look, sound and light. One volley can only clash once, and bots deal 40% of what a player does.
- Reduced motion and Effects at zero keep the headline and damage number without the flashes, particles or camera shake. Attack warnings stay visible.

## Boss effects

- Trails behave like gas left hanging in the air. They stay where they were laid, drift on the wind and spread out as they fade, rather than following the round around like a sticker.
- Bosses leave engine exhaust from where their engines actually are.
- Fire no longer shows faint stripes, and the flame stream holds together in flight.
- The plasma beam curves where it bends instead of folding at the joints.
- The boss bar and the **BOSS INCOMING** and **BOSS DEFEATED** banners are redrawn. The bar shows what the boss is doing, and turns red when it's after you.

## Arena Workshop

- Twenty particle presets, including Flame, Steam, Bubbles, Confetti, Leaves, Ash, Magic, Energy, Blizzard and Pollen. The inspector previews the effect, highlights its preset and shows how many particles are alive.
- Smooth particle sprites at four sizes, feathered rings, motion-stretched sparks, soft light and hot cores. Colors blend through natural intermediate shades. Reduced motion keeps its still preview and disables map particles during play.
- Sixteen widget looks, including Blueprint, Graphite, Signal and Rose. **Copy look** and **Paste look** share a design without replacing text, choices, board cells or logic.
- Widget drawing reuses mesh storage. Inspector previews stop drawing while scrolled out of view.
- Random signals can avoid the previous pick, shuffle every channel once, or pick by weight. Weight bars show each channel's chance; a trigger can send several distinct picks.
- Chance conditions roll a percentage when the trigger attempts to act, including percentages read from counters.
- Twenty more sound presets, with pitch, variation, repeats, timing and Near, Far, Everywhere or Cause audiences. **Hear it** previews the configured cue. Repeated sounds leave room for newly triggered cues.
- Ready-made loot-table, shuffle, pickup and countdown pieces demonstrate the new controls. The [editor guide](https://github.com/RobertFlexx/tankyard/blob/v2.0.5/docs/map-editor.md) covers every setting.

## Staff tools and fixes

- Server staff get a searchable player list, masked ban review and lifting, live server health, and boss summon and dismiss controls. Every action uses the server's existing permissions.
- Lifting a ban restores the address ban if its linked account record can't be saved. Reading server health doesn't fill the audit log.
- Creator tools add boss-health presets, heal-all and jumping beside a living player. Reason and duration presets, unmute and clearer player details improve moderation.
- Fixed the Mods row switch losing its click to the row beneath it. The detail button still works.
- Fixed Unlock becoming unclickable after focusing the password field. Show/Hide and keypad Enter work there too.

Signed staff packs stay portable. Existing packs unlock the updated client, and their passwords and identities don't change.

## Security

- Private server passwords can only be guessed a limited number of times per address, with more room for shared relay addresses.
- One address can no longer fill the party relay's rooms or a WebSocket relay's connections and lock everyone else out.
- Names and chat can't be made of invisible characters, so nobody turns up as a blank on the leaderboard or as a perfect copy of someone else's name.

## Compatibility

This release stays on **protocol 34**, so 2.0 clients and servers keep playing together.

- Railgunner, clashes and the new staff tools come from the server, which needs to run 2.0.5 to have them.
- A 2.0.4 client on a 2.0.5 server sees Railgunner as a very large Siege Engine and a clash as an ordinary parry. Clients older than 2.0.4 still have the boss-timer disconnect that release fixed, so they should update.
- A saved map that names Railgunner needs a 2.0.5 host.

New map logic and sound settings need a 2.0.5 host. Older clients hear a classic fallback for the new sounds. Existing map packs, Luau scripts, settings and staff packs carry over. See [playing](https://github.com/RobertFlexx/tankyard/blob/v2.0.5/docs/playing.md), [staff administration](https://github.com/RobertFlexx/tankyard/blob/v2.0.5/docs/creator-administration.md) and [server upgrades](https://github.com/RobertFlexx/tankyard/blob/v2.0.5/docs/central-pi-upgrade.md).
